extracted.intended_audience: patent owners, patent practitioners, PTAB judges, and USPTO examiners
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on when and how patent owners may seek amendments through reissue or reexamination in view of parallel AIA trial proceedings, and the factors the Office and Board consider when staying, suspending, lifting, or denying parallel proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing for filing reissue or reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office will consider a reissue application or a request for reexamination any time before, but not after, either: (1) Office issues a certificate that cancels all claims of a patent, or (2) Federal Circuit issues a mandate in relation to a decision that finds all claims of a patent are invalid or unpatentable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent owners may avail themselves of a reissue application or request for reexamination before, during, or after an AIA trial concludes with a FWD, as long as the application or request is timely filed. Example: a PO may file within 63 days of a FWD. Actions by the Office depend on filing timing and other facts. Continue to consult statutes, regulations, case law, and the MPEP.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trigger for issuing a trial certificate
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office will not issue a trial certificate (e.g., canceling all claims) relating to a patent at issue in an AIA proceeding until after either: (1) the deadline for filing a notice of appeal to the Federal Circuit has passed without an appeal (63 days after a FWD or 63 days after a decision on rehearing), or (2) all decisions or determinations in relation to an appeal to the Federal Circuit regarding the patent are finally resolved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Issuance of a trial certificate signifies completion of an AIA proceeding and automatically lifts a stay entered pending completion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reissue: statutory error requirement (35 U.S.C. § 251)
rubrics_metrics.description: 35 U.S.C. § 251 requires an 'error' for reissue; the error requirement is satisfied by a patent owner's failure to previously present narrower claims (e.g., In re Tanaka).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No admissions as to patentability of original claims are required. The oath may include a statement about an error related to failure to earlier present narrower claims (see MPEP 1414(II)). A reissue proceeds through examination similar to an original patent application and may be stayed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of filing a reissue application (37 CFR § 1.178(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: An application for reissue of a patent constitutes an offer to surrender that patent, and the surrender shall take effect upon reissue of the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A patent owner may abandon a reissue application at any time before reissue (for example, after obtaining a favorable FWD or on appeal). Before reissuance, the original patent remains in effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Third-party notice and protest opportunity for reissue
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office provides third party notice (by announcement of the reissue application in the Official Gazette) and a limited opportunity for a third party to be heard (by filing a protest).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 35 U.S.C. § 315(b) bar triggered by service of an infringement complaint on the original patent may not apply to the reissued patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ex parte reexamination: substantial new question (SNQ) requirement (35 U.S.C. § 303)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director must determine whether a request for reexamination raises 'a substantial new question [SNQ] of patentability affecting any claim of the patent concerned.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SNQ is not raised if the question of patentability was already decided in an earlier concluded examination or review (MPEP 2242(I)). Once an SNQ is established for existing claims, a SNQ is not needed for new or amended claims. The reexamination request should be decided on the wording of the patent claims in effect at the time (MPEP 2221).

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations on SNQ in light of AIA trial FWD
rubrics_metrics.description: SNQ cannot be a question raised in a ground already decided in a FWD. A later-filed request must have an SNQ different than that addressed in the FWD. SNQ cannot be established based on new questions raised in relation to amended claims proposed during reexamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prior to issuance of a FWD, an SNQ may be established based on a question raised in a ground presented in an AIA petition (MPEP 2242(I)). If granted, the Office may stay the reexamination pending the FWD.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reissue vs. reexamination — procedural and substantive scope differences
rubrics_metrics.description: Reexamination results in issuance of a certificate in the original patent, whereas reissue issues a new patent. Reissue may address all patentability requirements (35 U.S.C. §§ 101, 102, 103, 112); reexamination generally addresses only §§ 102 and 103, and § 112 only in limited circumstances for newly added subject matter. Reexamination must be based on patents and printed publications (35 U.S.C. §§ 301, 302).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: § 315(b) one-year bar triggered by service of an infringement complaint may apply to a reexamined patent even if reexamination involves amended claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director/Board authority to stay/suspend parallel proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director has authority to determine approach regarding stays of a reissue or ex parte reexamination during the pendency of an AIA trial (35 U.S.C. §§ 315(d), 325(d)). The Director has authorized the Board to enter orders to effect a stay, transfer, consolidation, or termination of parallel Office proceedings involving the same patent (37 CFR §§ 42.3(a), 42.122(a), 42.222(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Board ordinarily will stay a parallel Office proceeding where good cause exists; good cause may exist if an ongoing AIA proceeding addresses the same or overlapping claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing for Board consideration of motions to stay
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties may request authorization to file a motion to stay a reissue or reexamination, or a motion to lift a stay, at any time during pendency of an AIA proceeding. The Board typically will consider motions to stay a concurrent office proceeding (or may impose a stay sua sponte) after institution of an AIA trial proceeding and before the filing of a notice of appeal or the deadline for filing a notice of appeal to the Federal Circuit has passed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Motions can be filed at any time, but Board practice favors consideration in the post-institution, pre-appeal window.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-limiting stay factors: same or overlapping claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether claims challenged in a related AIA proceeding are the same as or depend directly or indirectly from claims at issue in the concurrent parallel proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a non-limiting factor; overlapping claim scope supports a stay because the AIA proceeding may address the same issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-limiting stay factors: same grounds or prior art
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the same grounds of unpatentability or the same prior art are at issue in both proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Overlap in grounds or prior art increases the likelihood the Board will find good cause to stay the parallel proceeding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-limiting stay factors: duplication of office efforts
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the concurrent parallel proceeding will duplicate efforts within the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoiding duplication of examination/review resources supports granting a stay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-limiting stay factors: risk of inconsistent results
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the concurrent parallel proceeding could result in inconsistent results between proceedings (e.g., whether substantially similar issues are presented).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Potential for inconsistent outcomes supports staying one proceeding to preserve consistency and administrative efficiency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-limiting stay factors: effect of amendments across proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether amending claim scope in one proceeding would affect claim scope in another proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments that would affect parallel proceedings weigh in favor of a stay to prevent conflicting claim sets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-limiting stay factors: timeline, stage, and statutory deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: Respective timeline and stage of each proceeding, and statutory deadlines of the respective proceedings are considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A proceeding that is more advanced or subject to imminent deadlines may counsel for or against a stay depending on circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-limiting stay factors: simplification or mootness
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether a decision in one proceeding would likely simplify issues in the concurrent parallel Office proceeding or render it moot.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the AIA proceeding can simplify or moot issues, staying the other proceeding promotes efficient administration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Denial of institution under 35 U.S.C. § 325(d)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board may deny institution under § 325(d) of a requested AIA trial proceeding if a parallel reissue application or reexamination proceeding is in a more advanced stage and involves overlapping issues with the proposed AIA trial proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advanced stage parallel Office proceedings with overlap can be a basis for denying institution of AIA trials under § 325(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Patents (Examiners) suspension of reissue (37 CFR § 1.103 and MPEP)
rubrics_metrics.description: Patents may suspend a parallel reissue proceeding either sua sponte or on request of applicant under 37 CFR § 1.103. Patents typically consider similar factors as the Board but weigh them based on facts at the time of suspension (see MPEP 1442.02). Patents typically will suspend when there is concurrent litigation or a pending PTAB trial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patents may or may not suspend if the examiner sees that the trial has been terminated, there are no significant overlapping issues, or if the applicant desires examination at that time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factors for lifting a stay — changed circumstances and PO actions
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board considers whether factors indicating good cause have changed since the stay was ordered; whether the patent owner has requested adverse judgment or canceled all claims at issue in the AIA proceeding; whether the patent owner is requesting rehearing of, or appealing, the FWD; and whether the patent owner agrees to abide by estoppel provisions in 37 CFR § 42.73(d)(3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also consider whether lifting the stay would be in the interests of efficient administration of the Office and integrity of the patent system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stay duration language and automatic lifting
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board generally will indicate that a stay will remain in place 'pending the termination or completion of the instant proceeding'. Absent a motion to lift the stay, a stay typically will remain at least until after the deadline for filing of a notice of appeal to the Federal Circuit has passed. Issuance of a trial certificate signifies completion of an AIA proceeding and automatically lifts such a stay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties should be aware that the typical stay wording ties the stay to the AIA proceeding's completion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motion to lift stay after FWD — meaningful amendments standard
rubrics_metrics.description: If a patent owner files a motion to lift a stay after a FWD, the Board typically will lift the stay, absent reasons not to. The Board typically will lift a stay if the patent owner proposes amendments in a reissue or reexamination in a meaningful way not previously considered by the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Meaningful amendments include those that narrow the scope of claims considered in an AIA proceeding or otherwise attempt to resolve issues identified in a FWD.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patents factors for lifting a reissue suspension
rubrics_metrics.description: Patents may lift a suspension of (or not suspend) a related reissue while an appeal to the Federal Circuit is pending if requested by patent owner after Board issues a FWD (or relevant rehearing decision). Patents may lift a suspension if the patent owner adequately shows that the reissue attempts to resolve issues identified in the FWD (e.g., meaningful amendments not previously considered, taking into account estoppel) or correct an unrelated issue (priority, inventorship, drawing). Otherwise, Patents generally will not lift a suspension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patents will weigh whether the reissue meaningfully addresses issues raised in the AIA proceeding before lifting suspension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office practice during Federal Circuit appeals — reissue
rubrics_metrics.description: After a FWD issues, as long as the patent owner files timely and raises issues different than those already considered in the AIA proceeding (e.g., amendments meaningfully different than a previously presented motion to amend), the Office typically will consider a reissue application (subject to possible suspension). If a Federal Circuit appeal remains ongoing when an examiner identifies allowable subject matter, the Office typically will not pass a reissue application to allowance until the Federal Circuit appeal concludes; the examiner may need to reevaluate allowance in view of Federal Circuit decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After appeal concludes, patent owner may proceed to issuance, file an RCE, or abandon the reissue application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office practice during Federal Circuit appeals — reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent owners do not have the option to abandon ex parte reexamination proceedings; once started, reexaminations proceed with special dispatch to completion (35 U.S.C. § 305). After the Office determines to lift a stay (or that a stay is inappropriate), reexamination typically continues to completion notwithstanding a Federal Circuit appeal of a FWD on the same patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the Office identifies allowable subject matter or determines claims unpatentable, it typically will issue a NIRC and reexamination certificate even if a relevant Federal Circuit appeal is ongoing, unless the patent owner timely files a notice of appeal in the reexamination for Board review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeals and preserving claims on appeal during reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: To ensure a reexamination certificate does not cancel original patent claims that are separately on appeal at the Federal Circuit, the patent owner must timely file an appeal of any final rejection of those original claims in the reexamination (to the Board by filing a notice of appeal within the required time).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent owners should timely appeal reexamination final rejections if those original claims are on Federal Circuit appeal to avoid unintended cancellation by a reexamination certificate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study findings (administrative context) — prevalence and timing trends
rubrics_metrics.description: Study results: 89% of patents challenged in AIA proceedings have not had any associated reexams or reissues. In 71.5% of patents that had both reexam request and an AIA petition, the reexam request was filed before the AIA petition. In 70.3% of patents that had both reissue and an AIA petition, the reissue application was filed on or after the AIA petition. There were about four times as many patents that had an AIA petition and a reexam request as patents that had an AIA petition and a reissue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These statistics provide context for how commonly parallel proceedings occur and their typical sequencing; they do not change legal standards but inform expectations.
